segs.en: In China almost everyone knows the stories of the “Three Kingdoms”.
The Three Kingdoms were Wei, Shu and Wu, three states that existed side by side in the third century AD and fought one another for decades.
This period lasted less than a hundred years, yet it has left behind more stories than many much longer dynasties.

zh: 在中国，几乎每个人都知道“三国”的故事。三国指的是魏、蜀、吴三个国家，它们在公元3世纪的时候同时存在，互相打仗，一直打了几十年。这段历史不到一百年，可是它留下的故事比很多更长的朝代还要多。

segs.en: Why is that? One important reason is a book.
About six hundred years ago the writer Luo Guanzhong wrote a long novel called Romance of the Three Kingdoms.
The novel is a great read and its characters are wonderfully vivid, so a great many people have read it, or seen it on television or on the opera stage.
But a novel is, after all, a novel.
The real history is recorded mainly in another book, the Records of the Three Kingdoms, written by the Western Jin historian Chen Shou.
Below we tell a few of the most famous Three Kingdoms stories, and at the same time look at which parts are history and which were added by the novelist.

zh: 为什么会这样呢？一个重要的原因是一本书。大约六百多年前，作家罗贯中写了一本长篇小说，叫《三国演义》。这本小说非常好看，人物特别有意思，所以很多人都读过，或者在电视和戏曲里看过。不过，小说毕竟是小说。真正的历史主要记录在另一本书里，就是西晋的历史学家陈寿写的《三国志》。下面我们就来讲几个最有名的三国故事，同时看一看哪些是历史，哪些是小说家加上去的。

segs.en: An Empire Falls Apart

zh: 天下大乱

segs.en: In the last years of the Eastern Han, the emperor's power kept shrinking, the court was in disorder, and ordinary people lived hard lives.
In 184 AD the Yellow Turban uprising broke out, and there was fighting all over the country.
To defeat the rebels, generals everywhere raised armies of their own.
After the uprising failed, these generals no longer obeyed the emperor and began seizing territory from one another.

zh: 东汉末年，皇帝的权力越来越小，朝廷里很乱，老百姓的生活也很苦。公元184年，发生了黄巾起义，全国到处都在打仗。为了打败起义军，各地的将军都有了自己的军队。起义失败以后，这些将军却不再听皇帝的话，开始互相抢地盘。

segs.en: Of all these men, the most capable was Cao Cao.
tok: Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north

segs.en: He controlled the north and kept the young Emperor Xian of Han at his side, giving orders to others in the emperor's name.
tok: Emperor Xian of Han, last Han emperor

segs.en: In the south, Sun Quan took over what his father and elder brother had built and held a large stretch of land along the lower Yangtze.
There was also a man called Liu Bei, who said he was descended from the Han emperors.
At first he had no land and few soldiers, and had to seek shelter with one lord after another; but he was very good at winning people over, and many were willing to follow him.

zh: 在这些人里，最有能力的是曹操。他控制了北方，还把年轻的汉献帝放在自己身边，用皇帝的名义来指挥别人。在南方，孙权接过了父亲和哥哥留下来的事业，占领了长江下游的大片地方。还有一个人叫刘备，他说自己是汉朝皇帝的后代。他一开始没有土地，也没有多少军队，只好到处投靠别人，可是他很会团结人，很多人都愿意跟着他。

segs.en: Over time, the forces of these three men turned into three states.
In 220 AD Cao Cao's son Cao Pi became emperor and named his state Wei.
tok: Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north
Cao Pi (187–226), first emperor of Wei

segs.en: The next year Liu Bei also made himself emperor, in Chengdu; historians call his state Shu Han, or Shu for short.
A few years later Sun Quan too became emperor, of a state called Wu.
These were the “Three Kingdoms”.

zh: 后来，这三个人的力量慢慢变成了三个国家。公元220年，曹操的儿子曹丕当了皇帝，国号叫魏。第二年，刘备在成都也当了皇帝，历史上叫蜀汉，简称蜀。又过了几年，孙权也当了皇帝，国号叫吴。这就是“三国”。

segs.en: The Peach Garden Oath

zh: 桃园结义

segs.en: The story of Romance of the Three Kingdoms begins with the friendship of three men.
According to the novel, when Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei first met, they felt at once that they got on very well.
Behind Zhang Fei's house there was a peach orchard, and the peach trees were just then in blossom.

So the three set out wine in the orchard and swore before heaven and earth that from then on they were brothers, who would help the country and protect the common people together, and live and die as one.

zh: 《三国演义》的故事是从三个人的友谊开始的。小说里说，刘备、关羽和张飞第一次见面，就觉得彼此很合得来。张飞家后面有一个桃园，那时正是桃花开的时候。三个人就在桃园里摆上酒，对着天地发誓：从此以后就是兄弟，要一起帮助国家，一起保护老百姓，同生共死。

segs.en: Liu Bei was the oldest, so he was the eldest brother; Guan Yu was the second; Zhang Fei, the youngest, was the third.
In the novel, the bond between the three brothers stays deep throughout.
Later Guan Yu was killed by Wu, and soon afterwards Zhang Fei died too.
Liu Bei ignored all advice and insisted on sending his army to avenge his brothers, and in the end he suffered a crushing defeat.

zh: 刘备年纪最大，是大哥；关羽是二哥；张飞年纪最小，是三弟。在小说里，三兄弟的感情一直非常深。后来关羽被吴国杀了，不久张飞也死了。刘备不听别人的意见，一定要出兵为兄弟报仇，结果打了一个大败仗。

segs.en: So was there really a “Peach Garden Oath” in history?
The Records of the Three Kingdoms contain no account of them swearing brotherhood.
The book does say, however, that Liu Bei treated Guan Yu and Zhang Fei like his own brothers, and that the three often slept in the same bed.
Guan Yu and Zhang Fei followed Liu Bei all their lives and were utterly loyal to him.
So the three really were close; but the orchard, the wine and the oath are details mostly imagined by later storytellers.

zh: 那么，历史上真的有“桃园结义”吗？《三国志》里没有他们发誓结拜的记录。不过，书里写到，刘备对关羽和张飞就像对自己的兄弟一样，三个人常常睡在同一张床上。关羽和张飞也一直跟着刘备，对他非常忠心。所以，三个人的关系确实很好，但是桃园、喝酒、发誓这些细节，主要是后来的小说家想象出来的。

segs.en: Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage
tok: three visits to the thatched cottage

zh: 三顾茅庐

segs.en: Liu Bei now had good brothers, but he still lacked someone who could advise him.
Someone told him that a young man called Zhuge Liang, who was extremely talented, lived at Longzhong.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: So Liu Bei took Guan Yu and Zhang Fei and went to invite him.
In the novel, the first time they went, Zhuge Liang was not at home; the second time, in heavy snow, he had gone out again.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu
Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: Zhang Fei lost patience and said they might as well tie him up with a rope and bring him back.
But Liu Bei would not hear of it, and went a third time.
This time Zhuge Liang was asleep; Liu Bei would not let anyone wake him, and waited quietly outside the door until he woke.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

zh: 刘备有了好兄弟，可是还缺一个能帮他出主意的人。有人告诉他，在隆中住着一个年轻人，叫诸葛亮，非常有才能。刘备就带着关羽和张飞去请他。小说里，第一次去，诸葛亮不在家；第二次去，天上正下着大雪，诸葛亮又出门了。张飞很不耐烦，说不如用绳子把他绑来。刘备却不同意，第三次又去了。这一次，诸葛亮正在睡觉，刘备不让人叫醒他，就在门外安静地等着，一直等到他醒来。

segs.en: Zhuge Liang was moved by Liu Bei's sincerity.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: The two talked for a long time, and Zhuge Liang analysed the situation of the whole country for Liu Bei:
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: Cao Cao in the north was too strong to fight straight away; Sun Quan in the east was firmly established and should be made an ally; Liu Bei should first take Jing and Yi provinces, and then grow step by step.
tok: Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north

segs.en: This conversation later became known as the Longzhong Plan.
From then on Zhuge Liang was Liu Bei's most important helper.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

zh: 诸葛亮被刘备的诚意感动了。两个人谈了很久，诸葛亮给刘备分析了天下的形势：北方的曹操太强大，不能马上跟他打；东边的孙权也很稳定，应该跟他联合；刘备可以先占领荆州和益州，再慢慢发展。这次谈话后来被叫做《隆中对》。从此以后，诸葛亮就成了刘备最重要的助手。

segs.en: Most of this story is true.
The Records of the Three Kingdoms state clearly that Liu Bei went three times before he got to see Zhuge Liang.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: Zhuge Liang himself later wrote, in one of his own essays, that Liu Bei had come to his thatched hut three times.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: The heavy snow and the waiting at the door until he woke, however, were added by the novel to make the story more moving.
Today “three visits to the thatched cottage” is an idiom meaning to invite a talented person sincerely, again and again.
tok: three visits to the thatched cottage

zh: 这个故事大部分是真的。《三国志》里清楚地写着，刘备一共去了三次，才见到诸葛亮。诸葛亮自己后来在一篇文章里也说过，刘备曾经三次到他的草房来看他。不过，下大雪、在门外等他睡醒这些情节，是小说加上去的，为了让故事更感人。今天，“三顾茅庐”已经成了一个成语，意思是真心地一次又一次去请有才能的人。

segs.en: The Battle of Red Cliffs

zh: 赤壁之战

segs.en: In 208 AD, having united the north, Cao Cao led a great army south, hoping to defeat Liu Bei and Sun Quan in one campaign.
tok: Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north

segs.en: Liu Bei's forces were small, so he sent Zhuge Liang to see Sun Quan and ask him to stand against Cao Cao together.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu
Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north

segs.en: Some of Sun Quan's advisers urged surrender, but the great general Zhou Yu argued that although Cao Cao's army was large, northern soldiers were not used to boats or to the southern climate, and could certainly be beaten.
In the end Sun Quan decided to join forces with Liu Bei.

zh: 公元208年，曹操统一了北方以后，带着大军向南方进攻，想一次打败刘备和孙权。刘备的力量很小，只好派诸葛亮去见孙权，请他一起对抗曹操。孙权手下有人主张投降，可是大将军周瑜认为，曹军虽然人多，但是北方的士兵不习惯坐船，也不适应南方的气候，完全可以打败。孙权最后决定和刘备联合。

segs.en: The two sides met at Red Cliffs, on the bank of the Yangtze.
Cao Cao had a great many ships, moored one after another and joined together.
tok: Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north

segs.en: Huang Gai, a veteran general of Wu, saw his chance and proposed an attack with fire.
tok: Huang Gai, veteran general of Wu

segs.en: He pretended to surrender to Cao Cao and sailed towards his fleet with dozens of boats loaded with dry grass and oil.
tok: Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north

segs.en: As they drew near, the soldiers set them alight; a strong wind was blowing, and the burning boats drove straight into Cao Cao's fleet.
The ships, chained together, could not separate in time, and soon the whole fleet was a sea of flames.
With many of his soldiers also sick, Cao Cao was utterly defeated and had to return north.
tok: Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north

segs.en: From then on none of the three sides could wipe out the others, and the three-way division was more or less settled.

zh: 两边的军队在长江边的赤壁相遇。曹操的船很多，一条接一条，连在一起。吴国的老将军黄盖看到了这个机会，提出用火来进攻。他假装向曹操投降，带着几十条装满干草和油的船开向曹军。快到的时候，士兵们点上火，那时正刮着大风，着火的船一直冲进了曹军的船队。连在一起的船来不及分开，很快就烧成了一片火海。再加上军中很多人生病，曹操大败，只好回到北方。从此，三方的力量都不能消灭对方，三国的局面基本形成了。

segs.en: In Romance of the Three Kingdoms, the greatest hero of Red Cliffs is Zhuge Liang.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: The novel has a famous story called “borrowing arrows with straw boats”.
Zhou Yu, wanting to get rid of Zhuge Liang, deliberately ordered him to produce a hundred thousand arrows in ten days.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: Zhuge Liang, however, said three days would be enough.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: On the morning of the third day thick fog lay on the river. He had twenty boats covered in bundles of straw, sailed them up to Cao Cao's camp, and had the soldiers shout at the top of their voices.
Afraid of an ambush in the fog, Cao Cao dared not come out, and only had his men shoot arrows at the boats.
tok: Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north

segs.en: When the fog lifted, the straw was bristling with arrows, more than a hundred thousand of them.
Zhuge Liang went back smiling.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

zh: 在《三国演义》里，赤壁之战最大的英雄是诸葛亮。小说里有一个很有名的故事，叫“草船借箭”。周瑜想害诸葛亮，故意让他在十天里做出十万支箭。诸葛亮却说三天就够了。第三天早上，江上起了大雾，他让人在二十条船上绑满稻草，开到曹军前面，再让士兵们大声喊叫。曹操怕雾里有埋伏，不敢出来，只让士兵向船上射箭。雾散了以后，船上的稻草插满了箭，一共有十几万支。诸葛亮笑着回去了。

segs.en: The novel also says that the fire attack needed an east wind, and that Zhuge Liang “borrowed” it by magic.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: None of this is history.
In history it was Zhou Yu who commanded at Red Cliffs, and the idea of attacking with fire came from Huang Gai.
tok: Huang Gai, veteran general of Wu

segs.en: What is more, the historical Zhou Yu was a generous-minded man, not at all as petty as the novel makes him.
As for “borrowing arrows” with boats, there is no historical record of Zhuge Liang ever doing it.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: An old book records a somewhat similar story, but its hero is Sun Quan: one side of his boat was hit by so many arrows that it was about to capsize, so he had the boat turned round to take arrows on the other side, and it righted itself.

zh: 小说里还说，火攻需要东风，是诸葛亮用法术“借”来的。这些都不是历史。历史上，指挥赤壁之战的是周瑜，用火进攻的主意是黄盖提出来的。而且，历史上的周瑜心胸很宽，并不像小说里那样小气。至于用船“借箭”，历史上没有诸葛亮做过这件事的记录。有一本古书记录过一个有点像的故事，主人公却是孙权：他的船一边中了太多箭，快要翻了，他就让船转过来，用另一边接箭，船就又平了。

segs.en: The Empty Fort Strategy

zh: 空城计

segs.en: After Liu Bei's death, Zhuge Liang helped Liu Bei's son Liu Shan govern Shu, and several times led armies north against Wei.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu
Liu Shan (207–271), second ruler of Shu

segs.en: The novel tells this story: once, after the Shu army had lost an important position, Sima Yi, the great general of Wei, came charging with 150,000 men towards the small town where Zhuge Liang was.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: There were only some two thousand soldiers in the town; most of the army was elsewhere, and it was too late to get away.

zh: 刘备死后，诸葛亮帮助刘备的儿子刘禅管理蜀国，还好几次带兵向北进攻魏国。小说里写到这样一个故事：有一次，蜀军丢了一个重要的地方，魏国的大将军司马懿带着十五万大军，向诸葛亮所在的小城冲来。那时，城里只有两千多个士兵，大部分军队都不在身边，想走也来不及了。

segs.en: Zhuge Liang came up with a bold plan.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: He had all four city gates thrown open, with only twenty soldiers at each, dressed as ordinary townsfolk and calmly sweeping the ground with their heads down.
He himself sat on the city wall, lit some incense, and played the zither quietly, looking completely at ease.
When Sima Yi reached the town and saw this, he did not dare to go in.
He knew that Zhuge Liang was always very cautious and never took risks, so he suspected an ambush in the town and at once ordered his army to pull back.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: And so, with an empty town, Zhuge Liang frightened away an army of more than a hundred thousand.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

zh: 诸葛亮想了一个大胆的办法。他让人把四个城门都打开，每个门口只有二十个士兵，打扮成老百姓的样子，低着头慢慢地扫地。他自己坐在城墙上，点上香，安静地弹琴，看起来非常轻松。司马懿来到城下，看到这个样子，反而不敢进城了。他知道诸葛亮一向非常小心，从来不冒险，就怀疑城里有埋伏，马上命令军队退了回去。就这样，诸葛亮用一座空城吓走了十几万大军。

segs.en: This is one of the most thrilling episodes in Romance of the Three Kingdoms, but it is almost certainly not true.

As early as fifteen hundred years ago, the scholar Pei Songzhi, who wrote a commentary on the Records of the Three Kingdoms, pointed out that Sima Yi was not even in that place at the time, so the event could not have happened.
The novelist wrote it into the book to show Zhuge Liang's cleverness and composure.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

segs.en: Interestingly, “the empty fort strategy” later became a well-known expression for a particular trick: when you are weak, you deliberately act calm so that your opponent dare not move.

zh: 这个故事是《三国演义》里最精彩的情节之一，可是它几乎可以肯定不是真的。早在一千五百多年前，给《三国志》写注释的学者裴松之就已经指出，那时司马懿根本不在那里，所以这件事不可能发生。小说家把它写进书里，是为了表现诸葛亮的聪明和冷静。有意思的是，“空城计”后来变得非常有名，人们常用它来说明一种做法：自己力量不够的时候，故意表现得很冷静，让对方不敢行动。

segs.en: The Three Kingdoms Today

zh: 三国故事的今天

segs.en: The Three Kingdoms era ended long ago.
In 263 AD Wei conquered Shu.
Two years later Sima Yan, a minister of Wei, seized the throne and founded the Jin dynasty.
tok: Sima Yan (236–290), first emperor of Jin

segs.en: In 280 Jin conquered Wu as well, and China was united again.
But the stories of the Three Kingdoms have been handed down to this day.

zh: 三国时代早就结束了。公元263年，魏国灭了蜀国。两年以后，魏国的大臣司马炎夺走了皇帝的位子，建立了晋朝。280年，晋朝又灭了吴国，中国重新统一了。可是，三国的故事一直流传到了今天。

segs.en: Many Three Kingdoms stories have turned into idioms and sayings.
For example, “three visits to the thatched cottage” means sincerely inviting talented people; “speak of Cao Cao and Cao Cao arrives” means that someone turns up just as you mention them.
tok: three visits to the thatched cottage
Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north
Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north

segs.en: Another saying goes that three ordinary people thinking together can match one Zhuge Liang.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

zh: 很多三国故事变成了成语和俗语。比如，“三顾茅庐”表示真心地邀请人才；“说曹操，曹操到”，意思是刚说到某个人，这个人就出现了。还有一句俗语说：三个普通人一起想办法，就能比得上一个诸葛亮。

segs.en: Three Kingdoms characters also appear again and again in Peking opera and many regional operas.
Because of his loyalty and courage, Guan Yu later came to be worshipped as a god; there are temples to Lord Guan in many places, and some shops keep a statue of him.
tok: Lord Guan (Guan Yu as a god)
Lord Guan (Guan Yu as a god)

segs.en: In modern times the stories have been made into TV series and films, and into comics and video games too.
The stories are popular in Japan, Korea and Vietnam as well, and many young people abroad first meet Cao Cao, Liu Bei and Zhuge Liang through games.
tok: Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north
Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu

zh: 三国人物也常常出现在京剧和各种地方戏里。关羽因为忠诚和勇敢，后来被人们当作神来尊敬，很多地方都有关公庙，有的商店里也放着关公像。到了现代，三国故事又被拍成了电视剧和电影，还做成了漫画和电子游戏。在日本、韩国和越南，三国故事也很受欢迎，很多外国年轻人就是通过游戏第一次认识了曹操、刘备和诸葛亮。

segs.en: In Closing

zh: 结语

segs.en: When we read about the Three Kingdoms, it is best to keep two books in mind: the Records tell us what happened, and the Romance tells us what people wished had happened.
In the novel Zhuge Liang knows almost everything, Cao Cao is the villain and Liu Bei the good man; the real people were far more complicated.
tok: Zhuge Liang (181–234), strategist and chancellor of Shu
Cao Cao (155–220), warlord of the north

segs.en: Perhaps it is exactly this gap between history and story that keeps the Three Kingdoms so fascinating today.

zh: 读三国的时候，我们最好记住两本书：《三国志》告诉我们历史上发生了什么，《三国演义》告诉我们人们希望历史是什么样子。小说里的诸葛亮几乎什么都知道，曹操是坏人，刘备是好人；历史上的人物却要复杂得多。也许，正是历史和故事之间的这种差别，让三国到今天还这么吸引人。
